answer: Sybil resistance here rests on a decaying stake: every identity that votes must lock a bond that only unlocks after long inactivity, and voting weight grows with time-at-risk, not headcount. Farming a thousand keys multiplies the bond a thousand times, while each twin starts at zero weight and waits out a cooling period; splitting adds cost without influence. The pulse of honest actors reusing one long-lived identity stays steady. On proven collusion the protocol slashes every pot, so the marginal cost of fakes stays linear against a flat gain: an ocean of velvet anchors sinks before quorum.
